# Contributing to SENTRY

Thanks for your interest in improving SENTRY. Bug reports, questions and pull requests are all
welcome.

## Reporting a bug or asking a question

Open an [issue](https://github.com/nerettilab/SENTRY/issues) and include:

- the command you ran and the pipeline version (`-r` tag or commit),
- the error message, plus `.nextflow.log` and the `.command.err` file of the failing task,
- your Nextflow version (`nextflow -version`) and profile (for example `conda`).

## Making changes

1. Fork the repository and create a branch from `main`.
2. Make your changes. Pipeline scripts live in `bin/`, Nextflow modules in `modules/local/`,
   and parameter defaults in `nextflow.config`.
3. If you add a parameter, add it to `nextflow.config` and describe it in
   `nextflow_schema.json`, so it is validated and shown by `--help`.
4. If you add a module, give it a `conda` environment file, pinning package versions so
   results stay reproducible.
5. Run the test profile and check that it passes:

   ```bash
   nextflow run . -profile test,conda --outdir results
   ```

6. Update `docs/usage.md`, `docs/output.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `CITATIONS.md` as needed, and
   open a pull request against `main`. CI runs the test profile on every pull request.

## Test data

The test profile uses the synthetic samples in `assets/test/`, generated by
`assets/test/make_test_data.py`. If you change what the test data must contain, update the
script and regenerate the files rather than editing them by hand.
